modules.learningObjective: Setting up the basic HTML5 boilerplate, linking assets, and creating the main game-container block.
modules.lesson:
The document head is the brain of your webpage. It contains metadata that tells the browser how to render the page, what character set to use, and how to scale the viewport on mobile devices. By linking your CSS file here, you ensure that styles are loaded before the content is painted, preventing a 'flash of unstyled content'.

Think of the head as a configuration file for your HTML. For example, you can set the page language like this: <html lang='en'>.

modules.title: Base Styling & Theme Layout
modules.learningObjective: Implementing CSS variables, flexbox layouts, and the dark-mode aesthetic for the game board.
modules.lesson:
CSS variables (also known as custom properties) are a powerful way to manage design tokens like colors, spacing, and font sizes across your entire application. By defining them in the :root selector, you create a single source of truth that makes theme updates effortless. For example, changing a single variable like --primary-color can instantly update every button and header in your app.

Flexbox is another essential tool for modern layouts. It allows you to align items along a main axis and cross axis with ease, solving complex alignment problems that used to require messy floats or absolute positioning. A simple example: `display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;` will perfectly center any element within its parent container.

modules.lesson:
Building a user interface requires careful planning of your HTML structure to ensure that elements are accessible and easy to target with CSS and JavaScript. By using semantic tags and descriptive class names, you create a predictable environment where your logic can interact with the DOM seamlessly. Think of your HTML as the skeleton of your application, providing the necessary hooks for your styles and behaviors to attach to.

For example, when creating a button, you might use a data attribute to store specific information: <button data-choice='rock'>✊</button>. This allows your JavaScript to easily retrieve the value 'rock' whenever that button is clicked, keeping your code clean and modular.

modules.title: Core JavaScript Logic & Event Handling
modules.learningObjective: Programming the game state logic, random choice generator, and button click listeners.
modules.lesson:
JavaScript logic is the engine of your application. By using event listeners, we can capture user interactions and trigger functions that update the DOM dynamically. This creates a responsive experience where the interface reflects the current state of the game.

For example, you can use `element.addEventListener('click', () => { ... })` to run code whenever a user interacts with a button. This is a fundamental pattern for building interactive web applications.
modules.task:
### Goal
Implement the core game logic to handle user choices, generate a random computer move, and update the game display.

modules.title: State Persistence / Reset & Final Integration
modules.learningObjective: Connecting LocalStorage for data persistence and finalizing the reset function for a polished user experience.
modules.lesson:
State persistence is a crucial aspect of web development that allows your application to remember user data even after a page refresh. By leveraging the browser's localStorage API, you can store key-value pairs as strings, which provides a seamless experience for users returning to your game. For example, you can save a user's theme preference using localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark').

Resetting state is equally important for maintaining a clean user interface. When a user clicks a reset button, you should clear the data in both the UI elements and the storage object to ensure the game starts from a fresh, predictable state. A simple way to toggle a class is element.classList.add('active').
modules.task:
Your goal is to finalize the Rock Paper Scissors game by implementing score persistence and a reset feature.

### Requirements
- Add a 'Reset Score' button to the footer.
- Implement `localStorage` to save and load player and computer scores.
- Ensure the game state (scores, hands, and result text) resets correctly when the button is clicked.
- Update the UI dynamically to reflect score changes and reset actions.

### Example
```javascript
localStorage.setItem('myKey', JSON.stringify({ score: 10 }));
const data = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('myKey'));
```

If you're stuck, check the hints and MDN references for working with JSON and Web Storage.
